analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: The holidays are the Super Bowl of retail
key_insights: Retail ex-auto spending ran about 18% above its annual average in the five weeks ending Dec 24 in each year of 2023-25, based on BAC aggregated credit and debit card data, with a peak of about +30% in the last of those weeks.
The next-largest seasonal peak in retail spending was around July 4th, when the 7-day average ran about 5% above the annual average.
BofA expects elevated airfares to weigh on holiday travel this year, and thinks this could boost retail spending rather than cause consumers to pull back more broadly.
BofA's 3Q GDP tracking estimate is unchanged at 3.7% q/q saar after September housing starts. Final sales are tracking 3.6% and PCE 3.7%.
BofA's official 3Q GDP forecast is 3.5% q/q saar, below the 3.7% tracking estimate. The tracking estimate is a mechanical aggregation of incoming data and is distinct from the official forecast.
Today's calendar: ADP weekly job growth, durable goods, Case-Shiller HPI, consumer confidence and new home sales.

sector_views.rationale: BofA expects higher airfares to push holiday spending toward retail goods, and retail spending historically peaks about 18% above average in the five weeks to Dec 24.

risk_factors: Elevated airfares could weigh on holiday travel spending.
BAC card data has selection bias and covers only debit and credit cards, excluding cash and checks.
